subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Stem cells from a patient's bone marrow are an example of:
questions.explain: Bone marrow contains adult stem cells, which can form a limited range of cell types such as blood cells.

questions.q: Where are stem cells found in plants?
options: In the meristems (e.g. root and shoot tips)
questions.explain: Plant stem cells are found in meristem tissue at growing tips, and can differentiate throughout life.

questions.q: A typical human body cell contains how many chromosomes?
questions.explain: Human body cells are diploid with 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

questions.q: What is the role of the cell cycle?
options: To produce new cells for growth and repair
To make sex cells with half the chromosomes
To swap genetic information between cells
questions.explain: The cell cycle, including mitosis, produces new identical cells for growth, repair and replacement.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a stem cell and a specialised cell such as a nerve cell?
options: A stem cell has more chromosomes
A stem cell is unspecialised and can divide to form different cell types
A specialised cell can become any other type of cell
questions.explain: Stem cells are unspecialised and can differentiate into many cell types, unlike specialised cells.

questions.q: In the reflex arc, what is the 'effector'?
options: The relay neurone in the spinal cord
The receptor that detects the stimulus
A muscle or gland that produces the response
questions.explain: An effector is a muscle or gland that carries out the response, such as a muscle contracting.

questions.q: Stem cells in plants are found in regions of active cell division called:
questions.explain: Meristem tissue, found at the tips of roots and shoots, contains plant stem cells that can divide throughout life.

questions.q: Meristem cells from a plant can be used to:
options: Make plants with half the number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Plant meristems can be used to clone large numbers of identical plants, for example rare or disease-resistant varieties.

questions.q: Which statement about the nervous system is correct?
options: It uses fast electrical impulses along neurones
Its effects last for several days
It uses chemicals carried slowly in the blood
It is controlled by the kidneys
questions.explain: Nervous responses use fast electrical impulses and are short-lived, unlike slower hormonal responses.

questions.q: What is differentiation?
options: A cell becoming specialised for a particular function
A cell dividing into two identical cells
questions.explain: Differentiation is the process by which cells become specialised for a specific job.

questions.q: Why might stem cells from a patient's own body be preferred for treating a condition?
options: They contain twice the normal number of chromosomes
They are less likely to be rejected by the patient's immune system
They are easier to grow than other cells
questions.explain: Cells taken from the patient's own body have the same genes, so they are less likely to be rejected.

questions.q: What is a stem cell?
options: An undifferentiated cell that can divide to form different types of cell
A cell that can no longer divide
A cell that has lost its nucleus
questions.explain: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells able to divide and differentiate into specialised cells.

questions.q: The two cells produced by mitosis are:
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: What is therapeutic cloning used for?
options: Creating a whole new identical animal as a pet
Producing embryonic stem cells with the same genes as the patient to treat disease
questions.explain: In therapeutic cloning, an embryo with the same genes as the patient is made so its stem cells are not rejected.

questions.q: What are chromosomes made of?
questions.explain: Chromosomes are made of long DNA molecules that carry genes.

questions.q: Why are reflex actions important?
options: They are protective and help prevent injury
questions.explain: Reflexes are fast and protective, for example pulling your hand away from a hot object.

questions.q: Which part of the eye changes shape to focus light on the retina?
questions.explain: The lens changes shape (accommodation) to focus light from near or distant objects onto the retina.

questions.q: In which type of organism does mitosis NOT occur in the same way described for body cells?
options: A bacterium dividing by binary fission
questions.explain: Bacteria divide by binary fission, not the mitosis cell cycle described for eukaryotic body cells.

questions.q: What is the main function of the fatty myelin sheath around many neurones?
options: To insulate the neurone and speed up the impulse
questions.explain: The myelin sheath insulates the neurone and increases the speed at which the electrical impulse travels.

questions.q: During which part of the cell cycle does the cell grow and copy its DNA and sub-cellular structures, before mitosis begins?
questions.explain: Before mitosis, in interphase, the cell grows, increases its number of organelles and copies its DNA.

questions.q: What is the role of a relay neurone in the spinal cord during a reflex?
options: It releases hormones into the blood
It connects the sensory neurone to the motor neurone
questions.explain: Relay neurones link sensory and motor neurones within the CNS, allowing the reflex to bypass the conscious brain.

questions.q: Which neurone carries impulses from a receptor towards the central nervous system?
questions.explain: Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.
